_comment: Champions: an ordinary monster that rolled something extra. game/elites.py
holds the arithmetic and none of the values, the way game/hazards.py and
game/rooms.py do.
*** enabled: false IS THE ROLLBACK, AND IT IS NOT HOW THE LAYER IS OFF. ***
Two switches, and the difference matters. This one is the content rollback:
set it false and no affix is ever rolled whatever anything else asks for.
The other one is structural and is the guarantee that matters to the
recorded balance grid: World() takes elites=OFF by default, so the campaign,
every test, tools/balance.py and game/autoplay.py all fight the same
monsters they fought before this file existed -- and they would even if this
said enabled: true. A run only meets champions if it opted in, which it can
only do once the profile has earned the unlock in data/unlocks.json.
So the claim is not 'the numbers below are gentle'. The claim is that
nothing the grid measures ever reads them.
*** WHAT A CHAMPION MAY BE: STATS, NEVER BEHAVIOUR. ***
An affix carries an attributes block, and Attributes.from_dict refuses a key
it does not know -- so an affix that summoned adds, or charged, or pathed
around a pillar is not something the loader rejects, it is something this
schema cannot say. docs/limits.md records that nothing in this game paths
around walls, and every arena is laid out around that; a behavioural affix
is the one kind that interacts with it.
KEYS
enabled     the content rollback, above
chance      per-mille of ordinary spawns that roll an affix
from_floor  the first floor a champion may appear on
bosses      whether a boss may roll one. False: a boss is already the
act's statement, and a prefix on it is a second one
affixes     id, name, weight (relative), hp (per-mille of the creature's
own health, 1000 changes nothing), attributes (the eight, in
their own units -- see game/attributes.py)
HEALTH IS PER-MILLE AND max_hp IS REFUSED. data/difficulty.json makes the
same argument about its own hp dial: one flat number means something quite
different to a rat and to a brute, and +20 health is a rounding error on one
and a different creature on the other.
*** EVERY NUMBER BELOW IS A GUESS. ***
Nothing has swept this layer, and nothing can while it is opt-in: autoplay
never enables it, so the sweep has no opinion about whether a 12% champion
rate is a spice or a wall. Same position data/rooms.json is in, chosen the
same way and for the same reason -- the alternative is an instrument that
moves the fixed reference on the day it gains the ability to measure this.
The rates are set against one figure that is not a guess: an ordinary stage
carries a mean of 12.2 enemies, so 120 per-mille is between one and two
champions a room, which is the density at which a mark still reads as
special. The affix magnitudes are deliberately below what a difficulty tier
does -- Hard is +7.5% health on every monster in the room, and these are
+40% on one of them.
